To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) FOXM1 is frequently over-expressed in ovarian cancer; (2) FOXM1 over-expression is associated with high-grade ovarian cancers; (3) ERK/FOXC1 signaling cascade is involved in the metastatic potential; and (4) FOXM1 inhibitors can be used as a novel therapeutic agent in ovarian cancer treatment.
FOXM1 is a novel target in advanced ovarian cancer and its inhibition by thiostrepton and U0126 could be a novel therapeutic approach in the treatment of ovarian cancer patients.
FOXM1 is a downstream target of the ERK signaling pathway, and that the activation of FOXM1 signaling cascade is a key event in ovarian cancer metastasis.

a potential new mechanism of FOXM1-mediated ovarian tumorigenesis.
a novel molecular target for the treatment of ovarian cancers.
the molecular mechanism by which ERK/FOKM1 signaling regulates ovarian cancer cell migration/invasion and the potential of FOXM1 inhibitors as a therapeutic target for advanced ovarian cancer.
